title: Profile overview
text: Sachin Ved Gupta is a McMaster University Software Engineering Co-op student focused on applied AI systems, AI agents, machine-learning infrastructure, simulations, developer tools, and product-oriented software. His recurring pattern is to take messy operational or human context, model it clearly, and build software that helps people make decisions or complete work. He has completed software engineering and data science internships at Nokia, Nokia Bell Labs, Shopify, Zipline, and Microsoft. He is strongest when connecting ML or agent technology to a concrete workflow rather than building a model demo in isolation.

title: Career throughline
text: Across Sachin's work, the same design instinct appears: model a complex environment, expose the right interface, and let software help a person act. At Nokia, that meant infrastructure provisioning and diagnosis. At Nokia Bell Labs, it meant grounding ML and agent systems in engineering knowledge and operational signals. At Shopify, it meant production recommendation infrastructure and debugging. At Zipline, it meant simulating an autonomous delivery network and making the simulator accessible through natural language. At Microsoft, it meant improving PowerPoint Web boot reliability and prototyping repeatable browser-agent testing. Student work extends the same pattern through browser agents, autonomous drones, educational agents, cloud provisioning, and AI-assisted storytelling.

title: McMaster Software Engineering education
text: Sachin is pursuing a Bachelor of Software Engineering Co-op at McMaster University from September 2023 through an expected April 2028 graduation. His learning spans software design, systems, algorithms, machine learning, compilers, cloud systems, and product development. His public working profile reports a 3.9 out of 4.0 cumulative GPA and a perfect first-year 4.0; those academic figures are self-reported and should be described with that qualification unless an official record is attached.

title: Academic achievements and scholarships
text: Sachin's profile reports a Provost's Honour Roll Medal, a perfect first-year 4.0, and approximately $10,000 in scholarships from OpenText and Rogers. These are useful signals of sustained academic performance and early external recognition. The current profile classifies the figures as self-reported pending attachment of the canonical records, so responses should preserve that qualification when exact verification matters.

title: Microsoft — Software Engineering Intern
text: At Microsoft in Vancouver from May through August 2026, Sachin worked as a Software Engineering Intern on the PowerPoint Web Performance team. He shipped boot and reliability fixes involving canvas centering, off-slide shape visibility, scroll behavior, comments-pane layout reservation, and visual popping. He also built a PR-aware browser-agent testing prototype that compared baseline and changed builds across realistic tasks and environments, producing recordings and reproducible issue reports. The shipped product fixes and the agent prototype are separate scopes; continuous production CI adoption of the prototype is not established. Resume figures include a seven-day run, 17 optimizations, 21 percent faster boot time, and 13 production fixes, but their denominators should be confirmed before combining them into one benchmark.
source_name: Career profile and public-safe Microsoft case study

title: Zipline — Data Science Intern
text: From January through April 2026, Sachin worked as a Data Science Intern at Zipline. His agent-related contribution was a natural-language Codex workflow around an operations simulator: the agent could generate configurations, run scenarios, return charts, explain results, and suggest follow-up analysis. Under that interface, he built an extensible discrete-event simulation of autonomous-delivery operations, modelling aircraft, charging docks, workers, partners, event timing, demand, weather, and failures. He calibrated parts of the simulation with historical data and built validation tooling for throughput, timing, utilization, and bottleneck diagnosis. The project connects an LLM agent to a rigorous simulation and real decision workflow, combining domain modelling, data calibration, developer tooling, visualization, and cross-functional decision support. Public explanations should stay at this architecture level and avoid confidential operational or business data.
source_name: Career profile and confidentiality-safe Zipline case study

title: Shopify — Software Engineering Intern
text: From September through December 2025, Sachin worked in Shopify's Recommendations Infrastructure and Shop app context. His work covered recommendation relevance, production ML inference and streaming systems, debugging tools, and multi-tier caching, with technologies including Triton, Apache Flink, Kafka, GCP, Bigtable, and DSPy experimentation. Resume-reported work includes a relevancy judge distilled to a one-billion-parameter model for more than ten million recommendations, recommendation debugging used by more than 80 engineers, and local-to-remote-to-Bigtable caching that made an advertised-product filtering path 11 times faster. Those numbers describe distinct workstreams: recommendations are not users or training examples, and the speedup applies to one filtering path rather than the whole platform.

title: Nokia Bell Labs — Machine Learning Intern
text: From April through August 2025, Sachin was a Machine Learning Intern at Nokia Bell Labs. He researched generative AI and predictive modelling for 5G or network workloads, and built retrieval and knowledge-graph systems over engineering sources such as JIRA issues, logs, and code. The work used combinations of LangChain, Pinecone, Neo4j, and LangGraph. He also developed agents that detected application failures and executed Linux recovery actions. The role connects research, knowledge representation, RAG, agents, and operational reliability. Source notes contain several alternative model and impact figures, so exact metrics should only be used after normalization against their original baselines.

title: Nokia — Software Engineering Intern
text: From April through August 2024, Sachin worked as a Software Engineering Intern at Nokia. He automated OpenStack virtual-machine provisioning with modular Python and Bash, built a Chrome-based log-analysis and status-visualization tool, worked across Linux and infrastructure APIs, and delivered a four-hour technical training session to roughly 65 experienced employees. His notes report a 98.3 percent reduction in manual provisioning effort and a 64 percent reduction in bug-resolution time. These figures are useful examples of automation impact but should retain their source qualification until the measurement method is attached.

title: McMaster Aerial Robotics — software and ML leadership

title: McMaster SumoBots
text: Sachin built an autonomous sumo robot and helped run a competition for more than 100 participants through McMaster SumoBots. Career notes report a 4–2 competitive record. The experience is early evidence of ownership, embedded programming, event execution, and practical robotics under time and reliability constraints.

title: StoryBook Memoirs
text: StoryBook Memoirs is a conversational family-storytelling product that interviews elders, structures memories, and turns them into an editable illustrated book, with voice-oriented interaction and export. It is one of Sachin's strongest founder narratives because the AI is tied to a clear human motivation: preserving family stories. The product has a public working artifact and current startup potential. Public descriptions should clarify team contribution and fork provenance rather than implying that every part was built alone.

title: InterfaceAI browser agent
text: InterfaceAI is an open-source browser agent designed to execute declarative tasks through planning, memory, DOM-first interaction, computer-vision fallback, orchestration, and a Chrome or web interface. It is a strong example of agent architecture because it treats perception, state, action, and recovery as a system rather than a single prompt. Sachin served as Project Lead through GDG McMaster. Public repository evidence supports the leadership role and project architecture, while exact ownership of individual components should be tied to commit-level evidence.

title: NKI Llama inference optimization
text: In the NKI Llama project, Sachin reimplemented transformer operations for AWS Trainium using the Neuron Kernel Interface. Career notes report a 1.13-times latency speedup. The project is evidence of lower-level ML-systems and performance work: understanding transformer computation, mapping operations to accelerator primitives, measuring latency, and balancing readability with hardware-aware optimization. The exact benchmark setup should accompany the speedup when discussed in detail.

title: LearnBridge educational agent
text: LearnBridge is an educational agent built around Google ADK and ReAct-style reasoning, connected to Google Classroom and Calendar workflows. It aims to help students gather course context and start assignments faster. The project is a useful agent-integration story because it connects planning to real tools and student workflows. A previously reported 80 percent reduction in assignment-start time needs a defined study method, so the product concept and architecture are stronger public claims than that metric.

title: StockSee
text: StockSee is a HackThe6ix-winning data product that links real-world events to stock-price movement with visualization and forecasting. It combines data collection, time-series modelling, an explanatory interface, and a web product. The project is best framed as an exploration and decision-support tool rather than as investment evidence; forecast limits and uncertainty should remain explicit.

title: MITI collaborative AI music studio
text: MITI is a collaborative AI music studio created for HackMIT. It combined AI-assisted music suggestions or generation with a real-time collaborative web experience and won a music-track award. The project shows fast team execution, generative-AI product thinking, and real-time React collaboration. Exact award wording and Sachin's individual contribution should be stated from the project submission when precision matters.

title: BusForecast
text: BusForecast is a BramHacks-winning project that forecasts event-driven public-transit demand to support surge-bus allocation. It starts from a concrete civic problem, connects external events to demand modelling, and presents the result as a planning tool. A repository and deployment exist, but city adoption or production use has not been established.

title: MakeCloud
text: MakeCloud is a natural-language cloud-provisioning prototype that translates user intent into Terraform for multi-cloud environments. It explores how an AI interface can make infrastructure setup more accessible while retaining a declarative configuration layer. It is a useful developer-tool concept, but it should be described as a prototype and not as production-safe autonomous infrastructure management.

title: QuantRL trading prototype
text: QuantRL is a deep-Q-learning trading prototype evaluated with a multi-year backtest. It demonstrates reinforcement-learning experimentation, environment and reward design, financial time-series handling, and evaluation work. It should be presented as a learning project rather than investment evidence, and any returns require the full methodology, assumptions, fees, and bias controls.

title: ShopFits
text: ShopFits is a Shopify Minis outfit-building project with preference capture, saved looks, sharing, and virtual try-on experiments. Public repository history includes Sachin-authored work on video try-on and fit-preview features. The project shows commerce product sense, mobile-oriented UI work, and generative or vision-based experimentation. Projected conversion effects are hypotheses rather than measured outcomes.

title: Hackathon and rapid prototyping pattern
text: Sachin repeatedly forms teams and ships working prototypes under short deadlines. Recognized projects include MITI at HackMIT, StockSee at HackThe6ix, and BusForecast at BramHacks. These projects span generative music, financial data, and transit forecasting, but share the same pattern: identify a concrete user, combine technical components into a usable demo, and communicate the result. Exact award categories and individual contributions should be attached to each project rather than generalized across the full portfolio.

title: Software and systems engineering skills
text: Sachin's software work spans Python, TypeScript and JavaScript, React and Next.js, Flask APIs, Linux, Bash, OpenStack, Terraform, cloud platforms, caching, data pipelines, testing, observability, and simulation. His projects frequently cross layers: infrastructure automation at Nokia, web performance at Microsoft, streaming and caching at Shopify, event simulation at Zipline, and full-stack product prototypes. The common strength is connecting backend or systems behaviour to a usable interface and a measurable operational outcome.

title: Startup and product direction
text: Sachin is exploring AI startup directions where agents or intelligent interfaces reduce friction in real workflows. StoryBook Memoirs is the most emotionally grounded current wedge: preserving family stories through conversational interviews and book creation. InterfaceAI represents a developer-productivity and accessibility direction around browser agents. He has also explored real-estate AI, but the strongest current positioning is broader: applied AI systems that turn unstructured context into useful decisions or actions. These are evolving directions rather than claims of a launched company or proven market traction.

title: Interests and community
text: Outside core engineering work, Sachin enjoys hockey goaltending, table tennis, sports, travel, hackathons, and technical community events. These interests add context to his profile and reinforce his preference for team environments, competition, learning in public, and building with others.
